note: After the original description in Hagen 1858, Monographie der Termiten (Linnaea Entomologica 12, p. 63); the original is a Latin diagnosis with a brief German account, written as a point-by-point comparison with Calotermes nodulosus. Hagen described only the alate and saw 4 identical dry specimens, collected by Rev. Clark near Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, at Constancia, and held in the British Museum. The original record was placed in Calotermes (Calotermes rugosus), now referred to Rugitermes. Hagen noted that this species may be the black-thorax form of C. nodulosus, but kept them separate because their characters differ.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate pitch black, extremely similar to C. nodulosus but with darker wings. It differs in that the head is somewhat stouter than in nodulosus, dull, with fine granular sculpture, and the anterior impression is stronger; the pronotum is slightly wider than the head, likewise dull and with fine sculpture, the anterior corners more rounded, and the curve of the sides makes the pronotum slightly wider posteriorly; the 6th abdominal sternite of the female is strongly enlarged.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Pitch black; mouthparts, antennae and tarsi pale yellow, the tibiae and the 1st antennal segment light brown; wings as in C. nodulosus but darker. Extremely similar to C. nodulosus. The head is of the same shape but somewhat stouter, dull, with fine granular sculpture, and the anterior impression is stronger. Antenna 16 segments (whether complete is not known), as in nodulosus. Pronotum slightly wider than the head, dull, with fine sculpture, the anterior corners more rounded; the curve of the sides makes the pronotum slightly wider posteriorly. Legs as in nodulosus; the 6th abdominal sternite of the female is strongly enlarged. Wings and venation as in nodulosus but stouter and more distinct. Measurements: length with wings 10 mm, body length 7 mm, wingspan 16 mm.
